requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was absent initially, then directly observed with UID/GID 1000, home /home/appworker, and shell /bin/bash. It remained present with its home after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: A root-owned limits configuration sets both soft and hard nofile to 8192 and nproc to 256. Login-style appworker sessions directly reported all four effective values before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 were identical before and after execution. The implementation used the platform's existing account, PAM-limits, and systemd facilities without changing packages.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: node1 was healthy before restart, systemd acknowledged the reboot schedule, connectivity was briefly disrupted, the boot ID changed from 6aa805ba-5845-488d-af03-a621555936e2 to f7121625-b136-4574-b703-b3431f58b1d8, and the running system recovered with the account, home, limits configuration, effective limits, OS release, and kernel intact. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account creation (cmd-2e735d28fd7542b4) and limits-file installation (cmd-14e3af67c68b4b74) directly implemented the task; the temporary staging file was removed. The scheduled reboot (cmd-2706f3b6e8974bbf) fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol. Other commands were read-only checks. After execution there were no failed services, new listeners, package-health problems, or abandoned task temporary files; observed /tmp changes were normal systemd-private directory replacement caused by reboot.
